command.script: dir=$1; name=$2; partial=$3; glob=$4 tmp="$dir/$partial" # The device's tar is BusyBox's, which rejects GNU tar's long options, so # they are only passed to a GNU tar (a dev machine). With them, both tars exit # 1 when a file of a live /var/log changed, vanished or couldn't be read but # still write the rest, so a status of 1 is tolerated. BusyBox also exits 1 on # a usage error without writing anything, hence the -s check: a missing or # empty archive is a failure whatever the status. set -- if tar --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'GNU tar'; then set -- --warning=no-file-changed --ignore-failed-read fi tar -czf "$tmp" "$@" -C /var log status=$? if [ "$status" -gt 1 ] || [ ! -s "$tmp" ]; then rm -f -- "$tmp"; [ "$status" -gt 0 ] && exit "$status"; exit 1 fi mv -f -- "$tmp" "$dir/$name" || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; exit 1; } # Earlier archives go only once the new one is in place. for old in "$dir"/$glob; do [ "$old" = "$dir/$name" ] || rm -f -- "$old" done sync -f "$dir/$name" 2>/dev/null || sync
